fieldValues.title: Discovery queries stay flat
fieldValues.decision_rationale: Every real-use question reported on srs#726 fits a flat conjunction with value lists. A boolean expression language makes every implementer carry a full evaluator and multiplies conformance cases (OData's `$filter`, required even at its minimal level). Flat queries keep fixtures enumerable and keep a query readable as a list of conditions.
fieldValues.decision_statement: A `DiscoveryQuery` stays a conjunction of filters. OR appears only as a list of values inside one filter (as `lifecycleStates` and `in` do), and exclusion only as a per-filter test (as `excludeLifecycleStates` and `notIn` do). There are no nested boolean expressions.
fieldValues.decision_scope: The shape of `DiscoveryQuery` (`ext:discovery`), including axes added by later RFCs.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: A general boolean expression (`and`, `or`, `not`, nested). Flat now with boolean trees named as a later optional profile. Leave each RFC to choose its own shape.
fieldValues.accepted_costs: "kind is email OR status is draft" cannot be asked in one query; a reader runs two queries and unions them. "Not archived, or no status" likewise takes two queries.
fieldValues.review_trigger: A real use that cannot be expressed as two queries. *Checked at:* each RFC that adds a DiscoveryQuery axis.
